statements.t: These operating segments have been structured to align with how we view and manage the business with the full lifecycle of our clients’ targeted environmental objectives in mind.
We expect that amortization of identifiable intangible assets and other acquisition-related costs, assuming we continue to acquire, will continue to be significant.

In connection with certain of our acquisitions, we expect to incur $6.2 million, and may make up to $7.0 million in aggregate earn-out payments between the years 2026 and 2027, of which up to $3.8 million may be paid only in cash, up to $2.8 million may be paid only in common stock and up to $0.4 million may be paid, at our option, in cash or common stock.
We have grown organically over the long term and expect to continue to do so.
We expect interest expense to remain a significant cost as we continue to leverage our 2025 Credit Facility to support our operations, share repurchase activity, and future acquisitions.
We have made and expect to continue to make investments in our business platform that we believe have laid the foundation for continued growth.

In addition to the impact of seasonality on earnings, our environmental emergency response business exposes us to potentially significant revenue and earnings fluctuations tied to large environmental emergency response projects following an incident or natural disaster or more broad scale events.

Earnings volatility is also driven by the timing of large projects and significant recovery projects that follow certain large emergency response incidents, particularly in our Consulting and Treatment segment, and the impact of acquisitions.

Measurement and Analysis segment revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 decreased compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to a decrease in field services revenues of $9.6 million, which included the impact of adverse weather conditions in the first quarter of 2026 and the impact of certain temporary regulatory waivers on parts of our air testing business resulting in…

Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased to 21.7% from 18.4% in the prior year period due to significantly higher margins in our consulting and water treatment businesses driven by project mix and improved operational efficiency in the current year period, and losses in the prior year period related to our renewables business, partially offset by decreases in high…

Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased to 20.6% from 18.5% in the prior year period due to significantly higher margins in our consulting and water treatment businesses driven by project mix and improved operational efficiency in the current year period, and losses in the prior year period related to our renewables business.

We expect to incur $6.2 million, and may make up to $7.0 million in aggregate earn-out payments between the years 2026 and 2027 in connection with certain of our acquisitions of which up to $3.8 million may be paid only in cash, up to $2.8 million may be paid only in common stock and up to $0.4 million may be paid in cash or, at our option, in common stock.

We expect to continue to fund our liquidity requirements, including any cash earn-out payments that may be required in connection with acquisitions, through cash generated from operations and borrowings under our 2025 Credit Facility.

Strong growth in core consulting and water treatment services reinforces the underlying demand for our solutions, while improved project execution, favorable business mix and cost discipline are strengthening the profitability of our platform.
We expect to continue our acquisition strategy, while maintaining our leverage goals.”

As we look to the future, based on commercial and operational initiatives currently underway, we expect to achieve compound annual growth in revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of ~15% and ~25%, respectively, through 2030.”
